history_findings: Onset of erectile dysfunction coincides with propranolol use

differential.diagnosis: Erectile dysfunction secondary to vascular disease

additional_considerations.rationale: Psychogenic causes reduce libido and erections but usually spare nocturnal or morning erections, which are absent here; he denies other depressive symptoms, though his feelings about his mother in a nursing home may deserve exploration.
Fibrous plaque of the tunica albuginea can cause penile scarring and erectile dysfunction.

leakage_check.reason: A friend's attribution of the sexual problems to propranolol points directly at the rank-1 diagnosis (medication-induced erectile dysfunction); it is scripted history the SP gives, so it is kept.

source_issues: Age conflict: the opening scenario says 50 years old; the raw Patient Description and the note HPI say 54. demographics.age uses the opening scenario (50).

Exam line e009 says 'bilateral Babinski sign present'. Read literally this is an abnormal (upgoing) plantar response, which fits poorly with an otherwise normal lower-extremity neuro exam and is not mentioned in the gold; it is kept neutral in x021 (direction not stated).
The note says 'VS: within normal limits' (e002), but the doorway BP is 135/88 mm Hg, above the 130/80 target named in the sample closure.
The raw Patient Description says the patient 'appears anxious', but he denies anxiety and stress (p016).
p002 'my blood pressure is still elevated' is ambiguous in time (before or after propranolol was added); temporality set to unclear (f003).
Note PSH reads 'No, I do not.' (script wording copied into the note).
Gold rank 1 'Onset of erectile dysfunction coincides with propranolol use': propranolol was added 6 months ago and the problems began 4 months ago; roughly consistent.
The challenging question has a doubled opening quotation mark in the source; cleaned.
annotator_notes: The visit is a hypertension follow-up, so hypertension course facts (diagnosis, persistent elevation, home monitoring, last check) are filed as symptoms/hpi; the drugs are history_and_exposures/medications.
